text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government approves a plan to set up a $350 million Lebanon Toll Road Company.
- A group of 150 Lebanese nationals escaping the week-long political and ethnic fighting in Congo's capital Brazzaville arrive in Beirut.
- A pro-Iranian Hizbollah rocket attack wounds one pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militiaman in south Lebanon.
- High-ranking general security officer tells four parliamentary committees that the security service taps a limited number of telephones.
- Leftist labour leader Elias Abou Rizk reasserts the legality of his presidency of the divided labour union.
- Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri heads to Damascus today in an official visit.
- Beirut will host the 20th congress of the Arab Lawyers Union in 2000.
- Parliament speaker Nabih Berri supports cabinet's decision to sharply increase custom duties on imported cars.
